items.title: Charles McPherson interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, September 9, 2024 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: So therefore this is what I mean. You have to be a little bit of a wordsmith. ... you have to have the Will Rogers approach, it’s this really simple language

ctx.x: Marvelous. I wonder if you’ve ever had a circumstance where you were the elder musician with wisdom and, much like Barry Harris, and you tried to pass that on to younger musicians who might have been on a very narrow path?

Yeah, well I do, I mean because I teach so I don’t teach it in a school, but I teach privately. And I teach, you know kids and, adults as well. And that is one of the things that I kind of learned about teaching is like the art of — you’ve got the craft of teaching and then you have the art of teaching. And really to me art is the higher level of what craft is. Because yeah, but anyway to make a long story short, I think this is when you start having a bunch of students you start developing — first of all you…

the door to open. The Aha! moment for the student. And that becomes like I think that’s a part of the DNA of a teacher. Because it’s not like you’re just dispensing data and information, you’ve got to do it in a way that it’s being absorbed and then that’s where you have to — there’s a little four dimensional chess being played there because you’ve got to understand how the mind works, how the subconscious mind, the conscious mind — you kind of have to understand the difference between craft, between art. And…
